This guide assumes the switch is new or has been completely reset. The switch’s operation light should be on and blinking, which indicates that it is using a default IP address. 

1. Make sure everything from the switch is unplugged, then plug in the AC power. 

2. After the switch is done booting (operation light blinking, all port lights will flash once) plug in your laptop to port 8 using an ethernet cable 
3. Google the switch model with “default IP” 
4. Take that IP and punch it in as your IP address for your wired NIC, but one less 
1. For instance, if it is 192.168.1.254 then do your NIC as 192.168.1.253 
2. When you hit OK it will pop a message and give you the default subnet mask 
5. Hit ok and save the config to the NIC 
6. Go back to browser and open the default IP you Googled 
7. It may take a moment to load but should pull up the Cisco sign in page. If it does not, troubleshoot if the switch was correctly wiped to factory default, or double check NIC IP config 
8. Log in with default creds cisco/cisco 
9. It will prompt you to set new creds. Find these in 1pass. Use most up to date creds. 
10. Go to the settings to change the switch’s IP (usually right on the opening page under getting started or initial setup) 
1. “change device IP address” 
11. Set a NEW default static IP address by pressing the plus icon. Should be in this format: 10.25.254.XXX with subnet mask 255.255.0.0 
12. Hit save. 
13. The screen will now freeze. You will know it was successful if the operation light on the front of the switch has stopped blinking and gone solid green. 
14. Go back to your wired NIC settings and change it to match the switch’s new set default static IP except one off 
15. Using the browser, navigate to the switch and log in with the new admin creds 
16. Immediately first thing, click the red floppy icon, flashing “SAVE” icon, or immediately go and backup the running config to startup and backup in settings. 
17. Set up VLAN membership as follows. Last port for admin. **NOTE PLC MUST POINT AT NEXT HIGHER LEVEL SWITCH AKA STACK ![](data:image/png;base64,)SAVE THE RUNNING CONFIG TO STARTUP AND BACKUP CONFIG AGAIN 
18. Pull your ethernet from port 1 
1. Plug drop into port 1 
2. Plug all others into the access ports 
3. Test each port with the HAL monitor tablet cable, OR your laptop to ensure you get wired connection to the domain 
1. If using your device, remember to clear the NIC settings to DHCP 
19. Check the stack to make sure the drop is also on VLAN 25 and set to trunk. 
20. If all ports give access, you’re gucci. Go back to the office and crack a Ghost to celebrate. If you aren’t getting network, check the drop’s connection settings (should be set to trunk and labeled correctly) on the IDF stack.
